jobs.title: Analyst, Munich
jobs.description:
About General Atlantic

General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create lasting value. Guided by the conviction that entrepreneurs can be incredible agents of transformational change, the firm combines a collaborative global approach, sector specific expertise, a long-term investment horizon, and a deep understanding of growth drivers to partner with and scale innovative businesses around the world. The firm leverages its patient capital, operational expertise, and global platform to support a diversified investment platform spanning Growth Equity, Infrastructure, and Strategic Solutions. General Atlantic manages approximately $126 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of March 31, 2026, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit www.generalatlantic.com.

Position Summary

General Atlantic is seeking an entrepreneurial-spirited Analyst to join our Munich Investment team. Analysts are integral members of our deal teams and play a vital role in supporting the firm’s growth and success. This role provides exposure to the full investment lifecycle—from sourcing and evaluating investment opportunities, to conducting due diligence and presenting to the Investment Committee, as well as supporting value creation initiatives across GA’s global portfolio.

Analysts are encouraged to bring curiosity, initiative, and an ambitious mindset as they work closely with senior team members across sectors and geographies. Analysts will gain hands-on experience in prospecting, thematic research, due diligence, deal execution, and portfolio management.

Responsibilities

- Build detailed financial models and conduct quantitative and qualitative analyses to support investment due diligence and portfolio value creation

- Draft investment memoranda and prepare presentations for General Atlantic’s Investment Committee

- Collaborate closely with Managing Directors, Vice Presidents, and management teams, as well as entrepreneurs, to support portfolio companies and evaluate new opportunities

- Develop investment theses and sector expertise through in-depth industry research, market mapping, and direct engagement with industry experts and consultants

- Perform proprietary research and analysis through calls and meetings with key industry participants, customers, and advisors to inform investment perspectives

- Gain exposure to multiple diligence workstreams—including financial analysis, customer research, valuation, and competitive benchmarking—across the full investment lifecycle

- Evaluate and execute investment opportunities across Europe and other global markets

- Collaborate closely with colleagues across GA’s global offices, drawing on shared sector expertise and regional perspectives, with frequent travel to support investment activity and cross-office collaboration

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Finance, Business, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; Master’s students also eligible

- 1-2 years of relevant professional experience in Investment Banking, Consulting, Private Equity, or Venture Capital

- Fluency in written and spoken German and English is required

Attributes

- Passionate about identifying and supporting transformational, high-growth companies

- Inquisitive and entrepreneurial mindset with a strong desire to learn and take initiative

- Superior financial modeling and analytical skills, with the ability to build and interpret complex financial models independently

- Solid understanding of accounting principles and business fundamentals

- Proficient in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, with the ability to communicate insights clearly and effectively

- Creative and solutions-oriented thinker with strong business judgment and professional maturity

- Record of outstanding academic and professional achievement, demonstrating drive and intellectual curiosity

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, comfortable engaging with senior executives and entrepreneurs

- Collaborative and globally minded, eager to work with colleagues across offices and geographies.

- Energetic, proactive, and passionate about investing and building businesses

GA Value

- Competitive compensation

- Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance plans

- Retirement savings plan with employer matching

- Professional development opportunities and ongoing training

- Collaborative and inclusive work culture with opportunities for advancement

jobs.title: Analyst, Real Estate and Data Centers
jobs.description:
About General Atlantic

General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create lasting value. The firm leverages its patient capital, operational expertise, and global platform to support a diversified investment platform spanning Growth Equity, Infrastructure, and Strategic Solutions. General Atlantic manages approximately $126 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of March 31, 2026, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit www.generalatlantic.com.

About Actis

In October 2024, General Atlantic acquired Actis, which now operates as its Sustainable Infrastructure business alongside its existing strategies in Growth Equity, Credit, and Climate. Actis is a leading global investor in sustainable infrastructure, delivering competitive returns for institutional investors and measurable positive impact for the countries, cities and communities in which it operates. Actis invests in structural themes that support long-term, equitable growth in defensive, critical infrastructure across energy transition, digitalization transition, and supply chain transformation. The firm’s decades of global experience, operational know-how and strong culture allows it to create global sustainability leaders at scale. Since inception, Actis has raised $26 billion to invest in a better tomorrow. Actis is a signatory to the United Nations backed Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI), an investor initiative developed by the UNEP FI. The firm has consistently been awarded the highest rating score in the UNPRI independent assessment. You can learn more about Actis at www.act.is .

Position Description

General Atlantic is looking to hire an Analyst to support the Actis Southeast Asia Real Estate team, based in Singapore. This is a small, high-ownership team investing in real assets across the region: the Analyst will work on live transactions from first screen through to structuring, financing, asset management and exit, rather than a single slice of the process.

You will build and own the models that underpin pricing and structuring decisions, run defined diligence workstreams with external advisers, and draft the memoranda that go to Investment Committee. The work is quantitative, commercially exposed and visible to senior members of the firm from day one.

Why This Role

- Ownership from day one. In a small Singapore team, the Analyst owns models, diligence workstreams and adviser relationships directly

- The full lifecycle. Origination, underwriting, structuring, debt financing, asset management and exit

- Real assets, real complexity. Development and operating risk, project-level debt, joint venture and platform structures, and multiple Southeast Asian jurisdictions — technical ground that compounds into a durable specialism

- Senior access and a defined path. Direct working exposure to Managing Directors and Principals

Responsibilities

- Build and own asset- and platform-level financial models — development and operating cash flows, project finance debt sizing, joint venture waterfalls and returns analysis — and run the sensitivities that inform pricing and structuring decisions

- Draft investment memoranda and Investment Committee presentations, translating diligence findings into a clear investment case with risks and mitigants set out plainly

- Run defined due diligence workstreams end to end — commercial, technical, legal, tax and insurance — coordinating external advisers, tracking issues to resolution and escalating what matters

- Support capital structuring and debt raising, including lender materials, base and downside cases, and covenant and debt service coverage analysis

- Maintain the team’s market evidence base: supply and demand, rents and yields, land pricing, comparable transactions, buyer appetite and exit routes across the region

- Conduct proprietary primary research through calls with operators, developers, occupiers, consultants and other industry contacts

- Work alongside Managing Directors, Principals and portfolio company management on value creation — budget review, capital expenditure tracking, performance reporting and asset-level initiatives

- Support origination: screening opportunities, preparing early-stage pricing views and keeping the pipeline current

The First Twelve Months

By month three you should be able to build a development cash flow model from a blank sheet and defend the assumptions in it. By month six you should be running a diligence workstream with limited supervision and drafting sections of an Investment Committee paper. By month twelve you should be the person on the team who knows the market data best and be trusted to take an adviser call alone.

Join our team and play a pivotal role in building General Atlantic’s real estate and sustainable infrastructure footprint in Southeast Asia. If you are a results-oriented professional with a passion for real assets and investing, we invite you to apply.

Qualifications

Required

- Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Finance, Business, Accounting, Economics, Engineering or a related field

- 0-2 years of relevant experience strongly preferred (investment banking or private equity preferred; consulting or relevant operating experience will also be considered)

- Superior financial modelling skills: able to build, audit and stress-test complex models from a blank sheet with minimal guidance

- Strong understanding of accounting principles and the ability to read financial statements critically

- Strong analytical ability, sound commercial judgement and professional maturity

- Advanced Microsoft Excel; strong PowerPoint and Word

- A clear communicator who can hold a view and defend it with evidence, and change it when the evidence changes; verbal and written fluency in English.

- Comfortable with regular travel across Southeast Asia

- Record of outstanding academic and professional achievement, high energy, and a real interest in investing

- Collaborative and intellectually curious about how assets, markets and capital structures actually behave

Preferred

- CFA Level II or Level III candidate or charterholder, or comparable evidence of quantitative discipline

- Exposure to real estate, infrastructure, project finance or another real asset class — including development, construction or operating assets

- Experience working directly with external advisers, lenders or joint venture partners

- An additional Southeast Asian language (Vietnamese, Bahasa Malaysia or Indonesia, Thai or Mandarin) is advantageous, but not required

Attributes we look for

- You check your own work, flag your own errors early, and understand that a number in an Investment Committee paper carries your judgement with it

- Proactive and low-ego, with a genuine willingness to pick up the unglamorous work

- A clear communicator who can hold a view and defend it with evidence, and change it when the evidence changes

- Intellectually curious about how assets, markets and capital structures actually behave

- Record of outstanding academic and professional achievement

- High energy, and a real interest in investing

- Keen to collaborate with colleagues across the firm globally

GA Values

- Competitive compensation, including a performance-linked bonus

- Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage

- Retirement savings provision in line with local statutory requirements and market practice

- Support for professional development and qualifications, including structured training

- Collaborative and inclusive work culture with opportunities for advancement

Process

Please apply with your CV and a short note (no more than half a page) on an asset, sector or transaction you find interesting and why. Shortlisted candidates will complete a timed modelling exercise and meet the Singapore team as well as senior members of the global Real Estate and Sustainable Infrastructure platform.

General Atlantic Life Sciences Practice

The GA Life Sciences practice provides capital and strategic support for development stage biopharma companies, with an established track record across public and private investments. The Life Sciences team focuses on novel therapies that provide substantial patient benefit and have the potential to redefine standards of care. GA’s differentiated approach to life sciences is characterized by highly thematic investing, scaling significant capital into companies as they advance through clinical development and commercialization, and partnering with management teams to generate value. Investments include Akero Therapeutics (acquired by Novo Nordisk), Karuna Therapeutics (acquired by BMS), Cincor Pharma (acquired by AstraZeneca), and Centessa Pharmaceuticals (potential acquisition by Eli Lilly).

Position Summary

General Atlantic is seeking a Life Sciences investor to join our New York‑based investment team. This role will have exposure to all parts of the investment process, including evaluating new investment opportunities and investment themes in biopharma and life science companies, conducting technical diligence, supporting deal execution, and working with portfolio companies. The ideal candidate will have a scientific background (MD or PhD) and at least two years of relevant industry experience, with the goal of driving strategic growth and generating value for the firm’s portfolio.

Responsibilities

- Source, evaluate, and recommend investment opportunities in drug development / biopharmaceutical companies including development and ownership of thematic focus areas

- Support scientific and clinical due diligence, integrating preclinical data, clinical trial results, regulatory strategy, and market dynamics into investment recommendations

- Develop and present rigorous investment theses to senior stakeholders, including the global Investment Committee

- Contribute across the full deal process, including coordination of third-party scientific advisors, KOLs, and commercial consultants

- Monitor portfolio companies and support the GA team’s efforts in capital allocation and value creation

- Leverage clinical and industry networks to generate proprietary deal flow and market intelligence

- Collaborate with professionals across the firm and foster exceptional knowledge-sharing

Qualifications

- MD or PhD in relevant scientific field (molecular biology, genetics, biology, chemistry, etc.)

- 2-5 years of post-graduate school professional experience, including at least 2 years of relevant experience in the life sciences sector (e.g., life sciences investing, life sciences strategy consulting, life sciences equity research / investment banking, biopharma operating role)

- Ability to analyze and integrate data from various sources into investment recommendations, including preclinical and clinical data, FDA/regulatory correspondence, and market research

- Strong foundation in financial modeling with a demonstrated commitment to deepening analytical expertise

- Passion for primary scientific literature, including scientific/medical meetings and conferences

- High degree of familiarity with drug development and regulatory processes

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize and present complex information clearly

- Demonstrated maturity and professional presence; comfortable interacting with senior executives and management teams

- Highly motivated, inquisitive, and a positive, can-do attitude

- Ability to take ownership, work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment

GA Value

General Atlantic offers a robust reward program to all employees that will support you and your family, maintaining fulfilling, secure and healthy lives now and into the future, which includes but is not limited to medical insurance, retirement savings contributions, mental and physical health resources and an equal pay program that allows you to earn a base salary of $150,000 –160,000   of which the exact amount offered will be driven by the degree to which you meet role requirements, additional special skills and experience.  Additional reward programs, such as annual discretionary bonuses and long-term incentive programs, are available for eligible employees and are offered as recognition for performance and one’s contributions towards the organization’s success.

jobs.description:
About General Atlantic

General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. General Atlantic manages approximately $126 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of March 31, 2026, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit www.generalatlantic.com.

Position Summary

The Transaction Support Group (“TSG”) team at General Atlantic plays an essential role in the coordination, execution, implementation and management of transactions throughout the life of a fund. This function will sit both in the Energy and Infrastructure asset class and the wider TSG team which comprises of three core team members. The objective of this role is to introduce efficiency to the entire investment process by supporting deal teams in navigating legal, compliance, tax and regulatory requirements during the origination, execution, investment management and exit stages. This position becomes a key ‘enabler’ and main point of contact between deal teams and other functional teams across the General Atlantic platforms (legal, tax, compliance, SPV governance, Funds services, finance functions), as well as external advisors where applicable.

Responsibilities

- You will be a critical part of the deal management function. This will require involvement on multiple levels including instructing legal advisors, assisting on internal approval processes, ensuring the set-up of our investment vehicles (SPVs), flow of funds procedures, execution of documents and director briefings. A TSG member must be able to grasp all facets of a deal and effectively communicate, coordinate and manage all the processes linked to a deal both internally and externally.

- Management of legal processes including non-disclosure agreements, term sheets, engagement agreements, briefing of external counsel and regular interaction with the General Atlantic Legal team as well as General Atlantic’s preferred legal advisors. Relationship building and maintenance with internal and external stakeholders is a key requirement for the role.

- Assisting in the coordination of compliance-related matters such as customer due diligence and other regulatory requirements which are implemented by the General Atlantic Compliance team and supported by our preferred legal advisors.

- Working closely with our SPV Governance team and our service providers who manage our SPVs in various jurisdictions including Mauritius, Luxembourg and Singapore to ensure transactions are concluded in line with TSG’s best practice.

- This is an important deal management function and you will be most effective immersing yourself in your asset class, your deal teams and understanding the intricacies and moving parts of each transaction including a high-level understanding (or ability to learn fast) of legal, tax, commercial and governance related matters.

- Presenting on the status of transactions at quarterly management meetings of the Energy and Infrastructure teams.

While this role description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, General Atlantic reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties from particular roles and assign other duties as necessary.

Qualifications

- A tertiary qualification which includes functioning legal knowledge and experience.

- Candidates with a legal work experience either as part of an in house legal team or group company secretary office in a medium to large enterprise will be preferred.

- Exposure to an international working environment, preferably gained in an inclusive and collaborative multinational company is advantageous but not required.

- Can demonstrate the ability and track record to learn and grasp new processes.

- Keen and quick learner with strong attention to detail.

- Track record in collaboration with external service providers and internal business units such as finance and compliance.

- Has a passion to learn and develop a career through collaboration and pushing boundaries in personal development.

- Independent self-starter who naturally takes initiative, can see the big picture while still maintaining focus on priorities and details. Roll-up-one’s sleeves attitude important.

- Strong written and spoken English. Excellent communication skills are essential.

- Excellent inter-personal, co-ordination and time management skills.

- Performance and results oriented.

- Ability to manage granular-level tasks and co-ordinate activities, diaries and manage stakeholders.

- Ability to prioritise own workload and meet deadlines.

- Ability to work well independently and as part of a team.

- Fluent written and spoken English.

- Highly analytical coupled with strong intuition; able to think and react quickly

- Strong project management skills – time management, pattern recognition, prioritization and strong judgement are critical; ability to work well under pressure without compromising quality

- Strong attention to detail, exceptional follow through and consistently delivers results

- Ability to work independently and proactively in a high performing global organization. Highly collaborative and capable of working effectively cross functionally

- Demonstrated maturity and professional presence; comfortable interacting with senior executives

- Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written

- Highly motivated, inquisitive, and positive can-do attitude

jobs.title: Investment Vice President, Mexico
jobs.description:
About General Atlantic

General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create lasting value. General Atlantic manages approximately $126 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of March 31, 2026, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit www.generalatlantic.com.

About the Team

General Atlantic has been investing in Mexico since 20 14  and  established  its Mexico City office in 2015. Over the past decade, the team has partnered with 14 Mexico-headquartered companies,  deploying  close to  $4B into  Mexico , and  building a portfolio that has created over 20,000 jobs and delivered  strong growth  across sectors ranging from fintech and healthcare to consumer and pharmaceuticals.

The Mexico team  manages a $5B+ portfolio and  operates  as a lean, high-conviction platform with outsized opportunity. Small and agile by design, the team is deeply embedded in its  portfolio  companies and the broader entrepreneurial ecosystem, with a  strong   local presence and long-standing relationships across business, government, and capital markets.

Recent investments reflect the team's ambition and range: Banamex, GA's largest growth equity investment in Mexico to date, and  Grupo Aguilas   – o wner of Club América and Estadio Banorte  – u nderscore the firm's conviction in  the region  as it enters a multi-decade ph ase of expansion fueled by innovation, entrepreneurialism, and technology.

Position Summary

We are seeking a full-time Vice President to join our Mexico City–based investment team. As a key member of the global platform, the Vice President will lead sourcing, evaluation, execution, and management of investments across Latin America, while collaborating with colleagues across regions and sectors.

Vice Presidents at GA act as central relationship owners for portfolio companies, drive investment processes end-to-end, and play a critical leadership role in shaping investment theses, developing junior talent, and representing the firm externally.

This role offers the opportunity to work closely with senior leadership at GA and with management teams across our global portfolio, helping high-growth companies scale and create long-term value.

Responsibilities

- Portfolio Management & Value Creation:

- Work closely with portfolio company management teams to drive operational improvements, strategic initiatives, and value creation opportunities.

- Monitor financial and operational performance, identify value creation levers, and support strategic initiatives (e.g., M&A, market expansion, organizational buildout).

- Contribute to exit strategy planning and execution.

- Deal Execution & Diligence:

- Lead and manage complex transaction processes, including diligence, valuation, structuring, negotiations, and closing.

- Direct Associates and Senior Associates in analyses, modeling, and materials development; ensure high-quality output under tight timelines.

- Coordinate third-party advisors, experts, and internal cross-functional teams.

- Prepare and present investment memos for internal Investment Committee discussions.

- Deal Sourcing & Thematic Development

- Proactively identify and evaluate investment opportunities in Mexico and broader Latin America through market mapping, research, and relationship building.

- Develop and refine investment themes that align with GA’s global sector strategies.

- Build strong networks with entrepreneurs, advisors, bankers, and industry leaders.

- GA Team Development:

- Mentor and coach junior team members, providing guidance and support to foster professional growth and development.

- Contribute to a collaborative and high-performing culture within the firm, promoting teamwork and knowledge sharing.

Qualifications

- MBA from a top-tier program preferred; non-MBA profiles with relevant experience will also be considered

- Bachelor's degree from a top-tier university

- 4-7 years of experience in growth equity, private equity; investment banking foundational training strongly preferred

- Proven track record of executing successful private equity/growth transactions from sourcing to closing; presenting to investment committees

- Experience working closely with management teams and driving value creation efforts

- Experience covering Latin American investments is preferred

- Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment

- Passionate about discovering interesting transformational up-and-coming high-growth companies

- Exceptional financial modeling, valuation, and due diligence skills

- Fluent written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish
